clue.text: Weak after illness? Iron supplements — this may relieve headache

indicators.note: supplements means the iron symbol is added into the illness-plus-weak string
after places the weak letter behind the illness word

parts.note: a fever is a bout of illness
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Someone feeble after being ill is told iron tablets will ease their headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weak' looks like an adjective about the patient but is just the abbreviation W; 'supplements' slots the iron symbol in ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverfew is a daisy-like herb long taken as a folk remedy for migraine.

clue.text: Kind of celebrity to publicise favourite politician

parts.note: an A-list celebrity is one of the most famous
to air something is to make it public
a darling is a favourite or pet

explanation.surface: A celebrity type promotes the politician they like best.
explanation.walkthrough: Alistair Darling was a British Labour politician, Chancellor of the Exchequer from 2007 to 2010.
explanation.definitionFit: Alistair Darling was a senior UK Labour minister and Chancellor of the Exchequer.

clue.text: Tip from professional card player?

definitions.meaning: a useful hint or piece of insider know-how
whimsically, a trick taken at cards by someone who plays for a living

explanation.definitionFit: Insider knowhow is a handy hint, and whimsically a won card-game round by a pro.

clue.text: Mum transported pig dealer to rural event

parts.note: mum, as in keep mum, means quiet: sh

indicators.note: transported means carried away, so the letters of pig dealer to are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mother gives a pig trader a lift to a country show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but means 'Be quiet!', SH. 'transported' rearranges PIG DEALER TO into EEPDOGTRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepdog trials are competitive herding contests held at agricultural shows in the countryside.

clue.text: Right steer?

definitions.meaning: in heraldry, ... means on the right-hand side
a steer is a bullock, and ... is a small Irish breed of cattle

explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic term for the right-hand side, and a breed of small cattle from Ireland.

clue.text: Something artists use to lighten edge of mural

parts.note: to ease a load is to lighten it

indicators.note: edge of here means the outermost, final letter of the word mural

explanation.surface: A painter tries to soften the border of a wall painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters prop their canvas on this wooden stand while working.

clue.text: Street artist's agent agreed upon annually during career

indicators.note: during means the two short pieces sit inside the rushing word

parts.note: to career is to rush along, to sprint

indicators.note: upon in a down clue puts the assent word above the yearly abbreviation

parts.note: ay (aye) is a word of assent
PA stands for per annum, yearly

explanation.surface: A graffiti artist's representative signs a yearly deal in the middle of their working life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upon' stacks the assent above the yearly abbreviation in this down answer, and 'during' drops the pair inside the rushing word. Spray paint is the graffiti artist's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerosol colour is the medium graffiti artists work with on walls.

clue.text: Henry breaks in to rob — unknown where trials are held

indicators.note: breaks in means the henry symbol enters the robbing word

parts.note: to burgle is to rob a building
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A man called Henry breaks into a house to steal, his identity a mystery, near a courthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Burghley House in Lincolnshire hosts famous annual horse trials (eventing). 'trials' suggests a court; here it means equestrian competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Burghley in Lincolnshire stages a celebrated annual three-day eventing competition for horses.

clue.text: Flash specials served in Heston Blumenthal's place

indicators.note: served in means the specials are placed inside the village name

parts.note: Blumenthal's restaurant the Fat Duck is in the village of Bray, Berkshire
S abbreviates special, so two of them give SS

explanation.surface: Showy specials are dished up at a celebrity chef's restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Bray is a Berkshire village home to Heston Blumenthal's restaurant the Fat Duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something showy, loud and vulgarly ostentatious.

clue.text: State support invested in modification of Snake

indicators.note: invested in means the support word is placed inside the rearranged letters
modification of means the letters of Snake are altered into a new order

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Backing is put into altering the Snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake' with a capital suggests a proper name, but it is just letters to rearrange; 'invested in' puts the support inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Rent prime spot in Cinque Port

indicators.note: prime spot means the first letter of the following word Cinque

parts.note: port is the nautical left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone lets out the best location in one of the old Cinque Ports.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cinque Ports are a historic group of English Channel towns; here 'Cinque Port' splits into C plus port = LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a split or fissure, just as a cleft is a crack.

clue.text: Suspect Yankee after half a joint's chucked

indicators.note: after puts the Yankee letter behind what is left
half here means the cigarette word is split down the middle, only one half surviving
chucked says the front half is thrown away, so the back half is what remains

parts.note: a spliff is a cannabis joint
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American comes under suspicion after half a reefer is thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' and 'chucked' throw away the front half SPL of SPLIFF, a cannabis joint, keeping IFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for dubious or of doubtful honesty.

clue.text: One deserting party tipping over wine-following a six-pack?

indicators.note: following puts the party and wine pieces after the muscles

parts.note: a six-pack is a set of well-defined abdominal muscles, abs
Con is short for the Conservative Party

indicators.note: tipping over means the wine word is turned backwards

parts.note: red is a colour of wine

explanation.surface: A party-goer upends the wine and leaves after one too many cans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipping over' turns RED into DER. A six-pack suggests beer cans but means toned stomach muscles, ABS.
explanation.definitionFit: An absconder is someone who runs away or flees, as a deserter does.

clue.text: Birdwatcher ignores temperature (hot) a frequenter of the sanctuary?

indicators.note: ignores means the temperature and hot letters are left out

parts.note: a twitcher is a keen birdwatcher
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A birder pays no heed to the heat while visiting a bird sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignores' drops T and H from TWITCHER. 'Sanctuary' suggests a bird reserve; it is a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A twicer is a churchgoer who attends services twice on a Sunday, so a regular at church.

clue.text: Musician beginning to crowd toilet — it's time to move

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of crowd
to move says the time letter shifts to another place in the toilet word

parts.note: a latrine is a basic toilet

explanation.surface: A performer starts a crowd for the loo, saying it is time to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' shifts the T of LATRINE to the end, giving LARINET.
explanation.definitionFit: In an orchestra a player is often named by their instrument, as in 'second clarinet'.

clue.text: Current cat loses last of nine lives

indicators.note: loses means a letter is taken away from the cat word

parts.note: a tiger is a big cat

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word nine

parts.note: is, as in exists, means lives

explanation.surface: A cat is down to the last of its nine lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' drops E, the last of 'nine', from TIGER. 'Current' is a noun here, a flow of water, not 'present'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tigris is a great river of Mesopotamia, and a river is a flowing stream.

clue.text: Sarah peripherally joins diners in cocktail on the rocks

indicators.note: joins means the pair of letters enters the mixed-up group
in cocktail means the letters of diners are mixed up
peripherally means the outer letters, first and last, of Sarah

explanation.surface: Sarah sits with other diners drinking a cocktail over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' and 'on the rocks' suggest a drink served with ice; 'in cocktail' mixes the diners into INREDS and 'joins' slips Sarah's outer letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something ruined or wrecked, like a marriage that has failed.

clue.text: Underwear Department probes young lady with large cup size

indicators.note: probes means the department letter pushes inside

parts.note: a girl is a young woman
E is a large bra cup size

explanation.surface: A store's lingerie section takes an interest in a well-endowed young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A girdle is a close-fitting foundation garment worn round the hips and waist.

clue.text: Face meagre English transport service

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock
arid means barren or meagre

explanation.surface: An English person puts on a thin face.
explanation.walkthrough: Dial-a-ride is a British door-to-door minibus service booked by phone, often for elderly or disabled people.
explanation.definitionFit: Dial-a-ride is a bookable minibus scheme for people who cannot use buses.

clue.text: Tender canine needs metal filling

indicators.note: filling means the metal goes inside the canine

parts.note: a dog is a canine
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A sore tooth needs a metal filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' and 'filling' suggest dentistry; the canine is a dog. 'Tender' means fond, not sore.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting means fondly loving, which is a tender affection.

clue.text: Fashionable shop for WAG

indicators.note: fashionable read as able to be fashioned means the letters of shop can be reshaped

explanation.surface: A trendy boutique for a footballer's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: WAG is British slang for a footballer's wife or girlfriend; Victoria Beckham, 'Posh Spice', is the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria Beckham, nicknamed after her Spice Girls persona, is the archetypal footballer's wife.

clue.text: See 7
See 4 Down
Atmosphere in Northern Irish city reportedly stern

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are spoken, sounding like another word

parts.note: the air in Derry, a city in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: The mood in a Northern Irish city is said to be severe.
explanation.walkthrough: Derry (Londonderry) is a city in Northern Ireland. 'stern' looks like an adjective but is the rear end.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear of a ship, and a derriere is a person's backside.

clue.text: Revolutionary ocean net naturally catches parts of crustacean?

indicators.note: Revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
catches says the letters are held within the words ocean net naturally

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A radical's sea net naturally traps bits of shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'catches' in the definition; it is the hiding indicator, so the definition is just 'parts of crustacean?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelers on the head of a crab or lobster are its sensory organs.

clue.text: Saw corroded in days

indicators.note: in means the corroded word sits between the two day letters

parts.note: D abbreviates day, so two give DD
ate, as in ate away, means corroded

explanation.surface: A saw rusted away within a few days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the tool but means 'went out with', as in seeing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: If you saw someone romantically, you went out with them.
